software.name: altdos
software.notes: Carries Microsoft FORTRAN-80 2.8 (FORT, FORLIB, RELCNV) and the newer assembler and linker, keeping the 1.0 ones as OLDASM and OLDLINK.

info.name: usage
info.value: Leave room above RAM for the loader; with RAM filling all 64K it stops with INSUFFICIENT MEMORY. Answer INTERRUPTS with N unless the console card's interrupt is connected. MNT 0, then DIR 0

software.name: altdos_1_0
software.notes: Carries Microsoft FORTRAN-80 2.8 (FORT, FORLIB, RELCNV) and the newer assembler and linker, keeping the 1.0 ones as OLDASM and OLDLINK.

info.name: usage
info.value: Leave room above RAM for the loader; with RAM filling all 64K it stops with INSUFFICIENT MEMORY. Answer INTERRUPTS with N unless the console card's interrupt is connected. MNT 0, then DIR 0

software.name: altdos_1_0a
software.notes: Besides the DOS editor, assembler, linker and debugger, this disk carries Microsoft FORTRAN-80 3.02 with M80, L80 and CREF80.

info.name: usage
info.value: Leave room above RAM for the loader; with RAM filling all 64K it stops with INSUFFICIENT MEMORY. Answer INTERRUPTS with N unless the console card's interrupt is connected. MNT 0, then DIR 0

software.name: dbasic
software.notes: The last Altair release of BASIC. Also on the disk: PIP, STARTREK, INSTR, ISAM-TWO and ISAM-T16.

info.name: usage
info.value: Answer LINEPRINTER with C, O or Q, then MOUNT 0 before FILES or LOAD

software.name: dbasic_300_5_c
software.notes: Still had some of 5.0's string space collection problems, which 300-5-F fixed. Also on the disk: PIP, STARTREK, INSTR, ISAM-TWO, SORT and ISAM-T16.

info.name: usage
info.value: Answer LINEPRINTER with C, O or Q, then MOUNT 0 before FILES or LOAD

software.name: dbasic_5_0
software.notes: Had string space collection problems and was not widely distributed. Also on the disk: PIP, BOMBER and 3DTTT.

info.name: usage
info.value: Answer LINEPRINTER with C, O or Q, then MOUNT 0 before FILES or LOAD

software.name: dbasic_4_1
software.notes: Also has programs from the Altair Computer Center in Houston, written by David M. Fogg in 1977, among them PIP 4.0 and games.

info.name: usage
info.value: Answer LINEPRINTER with C, O or Q, then MOUNT 0 before FILES or LOAD

software.name: dbasic_4_0
software.notes: Also on the disk: PIP.

software.name: cpm141
software.notes: Lifeboat's system release disk for the Altair, from which MOVCPM and SYSGEN make a CP/M for the RAM fitted. Its CONFIG.COM has been set to the 88-2SIO at 10h (configuration byte 0120h set to 0).

software.name: cpm141_48k
software.notes: A user's 48K system, patched for the 88-2SIO with USER.ASM, carrying MicroPro WordStar 1.00, MAC, SID, MBASIC, M80 and L80.

software.name: cpm22lb
software.notes: Lifeboat's full Altair release, with IOBYTE support, MOVCPM, CONFIG and SAVEUSER, sized for 48K. No Altair hobbyist had a copy until two turned up in 2020.

software.name: cpm22bur
software.notes: From the Burcon computer store in Houston: Lifeboat's CP/M 1.41 BIOS with the changes CP/M 2.2 needs, sized for 56K. Its MOVCPM was recreated by Mike Douglas and is not original. The disk also carries LADDER, OTHELLO, MBASIC, MAC, M80 and L80.

software.name: cpm22bur_48k
software.notes: The same disk sized for 48K.

software.name: cpm22b
software.notes: Mike Douglas's track-buffered rewrite of Altair CP/M 2.2, version 2.3 of 7 June 2020, with IOBYTE support, write verify and a disk select timeout. It reads and writes Burcon and Lifeboat disks. Sized for 56K; MOVCPM8 and SYSGEN resize it.

software.name: cpm22b_24k
software.notes: The same release sized for 24K.

software.name: cpm22at
software.notes: Mike Douglas's CP/M 2.2b with Altair drives 0 and 1 as A: and B: and a Tarbell controller's drives as C: and D:, version 1.1 of 23 June 2020, sized for 24K. MAME has no Tarbell controller for the Altair, so only A: and B: work.

software.name: cpm3
software.notes: Mike Douglas's port of Digital Research's CP/M 3 to the Altair 8-inch floppy, BIOS v1.0 of 21 March 2019, sized for 56K. Disk 2 has more Digital Research utilities and HELP; the build disk has the BIOS and cold start loader source and GENCPM.

feature.name: part_id
feature.value: Build disk - BIOS and loader source

software.name: cpm3_48k
software.notes: Disk 1 of Mike Douglas's CP/M 3 port sized for 48K. README.TXT on the disk explains resizing it with GENCPM.

software.name: dbgames
software.notes: A bootable 300-5-F disk with 75 files, most of them games: STARTREK, MEGATREK, CHESS, CHECKERS, WUMPUS, HMRABI, LIFE, LUNAR and HANOI among them. ROBOT100 is written for a VT-100.

info.name: usage
info.value: Answer LINEPRINTER with C, O or Q, then MOUNT 0 and FILES

software.name: memtest
software.notes: MITS's MTST row, galloping pattern and galloping column memory test, written for their 4K dynamic RAM boards, with its source, on a bootable Altair DOS 1.0 disk. Every circulating copy had one bad sector in the MTST source; Mike Douglas recreated it by disassembling the program, and added the DOS editor, assembler, linker and a copy utility.

info.name: usage
info.value: Boot as Altair DOS, MNT 0, then RUN MTST and answer ENTER DRIVE with 0. Addresses are octal; a large range takes a long time

software.name: musiced
software.notes: The MITS Music Editor, dated 16 November 1977, on a bootable Altair DOS 1.0 disk with BACH. It plays through a card at I/O ports 340-373 octal, four ports a channel, which MAME does not have, so it loads and edits music but plays nothing.

info.name: usage
info.value: Boot as Altair DOS, MNT 0, then RUN MOSEDT and answer ENTER DRIVE with 0. At the * prompt LOA loads BACH from device 0

software.name: rtcdrive
software.description: RTC Driver for Altair Disk Extended BASIC 4.1 (32K)
software.publisher: The Computer Store of New York
software.notes: Adds a time of day clock and a time limit to BASIC 4.1 through USR calls. It needs the 88-VI/RTC vectored interrupt and real time clock board, which MAME does not have.

info.name: usage
info.value: Boot it, then put dbasic_4_1 in drive 0, press a key, and answer MEMORY SIZE with no more than 32511

software.name: adventur
software.notes: Mike Goetz's CP/M version of Crowther and Woods' Adventure, with its data files, on a bootable Lifeboat CP/M 2.2 56K disk.

info.name: usage
info.value: Needs 56K RAM. AD starts it; it asks for three digits first

software.name: mitstape
software.notes: Tape images of MITS 4K, 8K, Extended and Disk BASIC, the DBL loaders and Programming System II, with WRTAPE to write them to cassette or paper tape through an 88-SIO at 6 and 7 or the 88-2SIO's second port. Boots Burcon CP/M 2.2 48K.

info.name: usage
info.value: Needs 48K RAM. TYPE CONTENTS.TXT lists the tapes

software.name: bascom
software.notes: On a bootable Burcon CP/M 2.2 56K disk, with MBASIC 5.21, M80, L80, LIB80, CREF80 and a sample program.

software.name: bdsc
software.notes: On a bootable Burcon CP/M 2.2 56K disk, with CC, CC2, CLINK and HELLO.C.

software.name: ccgames3
software.notes: BASIC games chosen from a menu, moved from their original IBM 8-inch format onto a bootable Lifeboat CP/M 2.2 48K disk.

software.name: cobol80
software.notes: Mark Rosenthal's working disk: the compiler and its four overlays, the runtime, L80, and the HELLO, PRIMES, SQUARO and RECOVR examples. Some distribution files were left out for space. It has no system tracks.

info.name: usage
info.value: Fit a third drive and put this in it, with CP/M 2.2 in drive A, then log onto C: to compile

software.name: cpmgames
software.notes: A bootable Burcon CP/M 2.2 56K disk with LADDER and CATCHUM from Yahoo Software, OTHELLO, CHASE, LUNAR, STARTRK and TICTAK.

info.name: usage
info.value: Needs 56K RAM. LADDER and CATCHUM need a VT-100 terminal; LADCONF and CATCONF configure them

software.name: kermit
software.notes: Generic CP/M-80 Kermit, which needs a BIOS with IOBYTE support, on a bootable CP/M 2.2b 56K disk (BIOS v2.2 of 10 November 2019).

info.name: usage
info.value: Needs 56K RAM. KERM411, then SET PORT UR2 to use the 88-2SIO's second port

software.name: sc2
software.notes: Installed for a DEC VT-100, on a bootable Burcon CP/M 2.2 56K disk.

info.name: usage
info.value: Needs 56K RAM and a VT-100 terminal; SC2 starts it. For MAME's H19 terminal (-s100:1:2sio:rs2320 h19), run INSTALL on a copy of the image and answer Y, A:SC2, K (Zenith), Y, A, Y

software.name: wordstar
software.notes: With SpellStar 1.0 and INSTALL, on a bootable Burcon CP/M 2.2 62K disk. WS.COM is installed for an ADDS Viewpoint terminal.

info.name: usage
info.value: Needs 62K RAM and an ADDS Viewpoint terminal. For MAME's H19 terminal (-s100:1:2sio:rs2320 h19), run INSTALL on a copy of the image and answer N, D, WS.COM, then 3 and X (Heath or Zenith H89/H19) on the terminal menus, U to keep each printer setting, and Y to the rest

software.name: hitchhik
software.description: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
software.notes: Release 59, serial number 851108. The disk does not boot: its system tracks hold the CP/M 3 loader but it has no CPM3.SYS. The status line is drawn with Heath H19 escape codes.

info.name: usage
info.value: Boot cpm3 with this disk in drive B, then B: and HITCH. The status line needs MAME's H19 terminal (-s100:1:2sio:rs2320 h19)

software.name: zork
software.notes: ZORK I (release 88, serial number 840726) and ZORK II (48, 840904) play, on a bootable Burcon CP/M 2.2 56K disk. ZORK3.DAT is damaged, its directory entries erased or blanked, so ZORK III only asks for its game disk.
